event: Monday of week three: the morning after the storm is washed clean, blue and cold and very still.
The mere is flat again, littered with branches; the fells are back, sharp, snow on the tops.
At the boathouse the swimmers are back on; you and Shiv swim out to the buoy through floating twigs.
"Better than a storm," Shiv says, hanging there. "Worse than a rock." She splashes you, grinning.
Bea's door opens as you come up: Kit comes out first, in Bea's jumper over her own black skirt.
Kit sees you and holds her chin up. "I'll return it," she says, of the jumper. Bea snorts.

pictured.coverAfter: She's in Bea's jumper. A big soft cream one, cable-knit, much too large,
pictured.outfit: Bea's big cream cable-knit jumper over her own long black skirt

event: The three of you walk to breakfast together across the drying quad, Bea in the middle, talking.
Amara, at the hall doors, watches Kit arrive from Thornfield in a cream jumper, and raises a brow.
"Ashworth," she says, delighted. "Wool. Cream. Whatever next." Kit walks past her like a queen.

pictured.coverAfter: She's waiting for someone, or pretending to, leaning on the doorframe in a camel coat
pictured.outfit: camel coat over a fitted black knit and black tailored trousers, braids up, gold hoops

event: In the top corridor a glazier from Kendal is fitting new glass in the end window, whistling.
Yusra stands by him with a list, her palm bandaged white; she sees you and lifts the hand slightly.
"Healing," she says. "Clean cut. You did right." Then, to the glazier: "Double-check that frame."
Ten: the Foundations lecture in the Long Room, on mending: why a broken thing wants to be whole.
Kit sits beside you; Lin on your other side, drawing the lecturer's hands in your margin.
Two: the Practice Hall; a cracked teacup on every bench, and the mending sigil chalked on the board.
The demonstrator claps for quiet: on Friday, each first-year casts a glim and warms a stone.
"Before the whole hall," she says. "One at a time. It's a test. Everyone passes who's practised."
Beside you, Kit's face goes perfectly still, and her hand on the bench goes white at the knuckles.
You try the mending charm; your crack closes halfway along, and stops, a seam you can see.
Bea's cup gets warm instead of mended; she stares at it. "That's the wrong spell," she whispers.
At the end bench, back to the room, Kit's cup goes whole in one smooth breath, without a seam.
After practical Kit walks out fast, across the quad and down to the shore; you follow her.
At the water she stops. "Before the whole hall," she says. "I'll freeze. You've seen me freeze."
"My mother will hear. She hears everything. An Ashworth who can't cast a glim in front of people."
You stand beside her at the water and say: then we practise being watched. A bit more each day.
"One pair of eyes," you say. "Mine. Then more." Kit looks at you a long time. "Yours."
Dusk: the empty Practice Hall, where you once saw her ring of glims through the window.
You sit at the far end, back to her; behind you Kit's glim rises, steady; you see its light.
You turn sideways, looking at the wall; she casts again, and it holds, a little smaller.
You turn and look at her. Kit draws the sigil, says the word, and freezes, her hand in the air.
Her face goes white; you keep looking, gently, and say her name, and say breathe out.
She breathes out. A flicker of light: half a glim, wavering, gone in a second. But it was there.
Kit stares at the empty air where it was. Then she laughs, shaky. "That was terrible," she says.
"That was the first one," you say. She kisses you hard in the dark hall, once. "Tomorrow," she says.
At ten Priya bursts into the Thornfield kitchen, back from charmcraft, glowing about clockwork.
"Amara came," she says. "To charmcraft. She hates clockwork. She said so. Twice. And she stayed."
Priya sits down very suddenly and stares at her cocoa. Bea pats her hand, quietly.
In 14 you write a list on the back of your timetable: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Kit. Hall.
Under it, smaller: Friday. Then, smallest, for yourself: breathe out.
A day at Hollowmere ends.
